title: Tiantai Mountain · Even Heirlooms Get Lost
summary: A mountain gust wakes the map's guardian and blows a hole in the family's faith in its infallible map. What you rescue is no sacred decree, but a map that can still be corrected.

S00-01.title: Tiantai Foothills
S00-01.summary: While you haggle with the driver, your family map sets off up the mountain. Your first great feat in the martial world: catching up with your own itinerary.
S00-01.objective: Ask the way uphill and sort out the old map
S00-01.result: You learn the route upstream. A gust blows the old map toward the shallows.
lines: At the foot of Tiantai Mountain, you unroll Grandfather's old map, hoping to find a respectable way up.
Follow the stream, cross the bridge, and head for Guoqing Temple. The mountain doesn't charge a fare. It charges your knees.
Put that on your cart and see how many customers you have left.
While you turn to haggle, a gust slips under the scroll and lifts the whole map into the air.
Oi! I haven't even left yet. Why is my route running away?
A fine map. Knows its own mind.
You grab your bamboo pole and chase it toward the shallows. The driver stays behind, pinning down the ink box rolling past his feet.
Remember the directions before you run! You can patch a map. Knees are another matter.

S00-02.title: Recover the Scroll
S00-02.summary: Your pole retrieves a soggy map and a flame full of self-importance. For a moment, you think you've found a pocket-sized grandfather.
S00-02.objective: Retrieve the scroll and meet Youbai
S00-02.result: The scroll is recovered. Youbai joins you, and you decide to check the old route at Guoqing Temple.
lines: Barely out the door and I'm washing the family legacy. Grandfather would be fuming.
You lift the wet scroll with your pole. A blue-violet flame leaps between two old notes and stops against your nose.
Grandfather? Why are you... travel-sized?
Hold the family reunion! I am Youbai, guardian of this map. Adding branches to your family tree is not my duty.
You came out of Grandfather's map. That calls for some explanation.
Generations have copied this map. Generations have corrected it. I watched them write, took a nap, and woke up to you giving it a bath.
On the back, you find old notes in several shades of ink. Youbai hovers over the crookedest one and urges you onward.
Guoqing Temple first! We'll check the old route. And stop calling me Grandfather. It adds centuries.

S00-03.title: Over the Ridge
S00-03.summary: Youbai declares the old map infallible. The bridge promptly drops a plank. You can save the elder's dignity or your own feet. Feet first.
S00-03.objective: Use shoeprints and trail markers to choose a safe path uphill
S00-03.result: Fresh shoeprints lead you safely over the ridge by the pine-root steps. You mark the broken bridge and the detour.
lines: Cross the bridge ahead. I remember this stretch. I could do it with my eyes clo—
Crack. The last loose plank tips into the gorge. You pull back your raised foot. Youbai pulls back the rest of the sentence.
Closed, you can still hear it collapse.
The bridge has failed to comply with the map.
The map is right and the landscape is at fault? Let's hear what my soles have to say.
The vine slope to the right is slick with moss. To the left, an old blue cloth marks pine-root steps. Fresh shoeprints show someone has already climbed that way.
Wait. No returning prints beside the fresh ones... That path should go through.
Now that sounds like evidence. Give me more of that, elder.
hints: Look for a route someone has used recently.
The blue-cloth steps have fresh shoeprints and no return tracks. The broken bridge and mossy slope are unsafe.
Choose the pine-root steps marked by blue cloth and fresh shoeprints.
options: Take the pine-root steps with blue cloth and fresh shoeprints
This time, Youbai checks the prints before nodding. You climb the steps and leave the broken bridge behind.
Trust the family map and jump across the broken bridge
Youbai stops you at once: I identify routes. I do not reassemble travelers.
Climb straight up the mossy vine slope
You test it with your pole. A whole sheet of moss slides loose. Your legs have no better eyesight than bamboo.

S00-04.title: First Fight
S00-04.summary: Animals have surrounded a mountain traveler's manuscript. You suspect a priceless secret manual, until you discover the pages once wrapped sesame cakes.
S00-04.objective: Enter task map 1-1 and defeat the animals at the story question mark
S00-04.result: The animals retreat. The traveler and his manuscript are safe. You learn that Guoqing Temple still keeps old route records.
lines: At the top of the pine-root steps, a breathless traveler runs toward you. His empty arms make a convincing argument.
Young hero! Two illiterate book lovers have surrounded my manuscript on the rocks ahead!
Book lovers?
A rooster and a weasel. They read with their mouths, not their eyes.
It seems your work has finally found an audience.
I wrapped sesame cakes in the pages! That's half a lifetime of roads, not half a lifetime of cake!
Stay somewhere safe and point the way. I'll retrieve the manuscript and discourage the readership.
Prepare before setting off. First lesson of the martial world: don't let the family map lose to greasy stationery.
after_battle_lines: The animals finally back away. You lift the scattered pages with your pole while the traveler catches them in his sack. The crumbs land louder than applause.
Manuscript intact. Author intact. Those two cakes can count as royalties.
Use oilpaper next time. Don't let your readers eat the ending.
I illuminate the way. Sesame seeds are outside my duties.
Guoqing Temple still has old route records. Compare your map with those. They're more reliable than my hungry mouth.
Good. First we fill in the map. Then we fill our stomachs.
hints: This step requires entering the task map. Protect the traveler and his manuscript.
Reach the story question mark in task map 1-1 and defeat the animals with your current party.
Win the task battle at the mandatory story question mark to secure the manuscript.

S00-05.title: Guoqing Temple
S00-05.summary: You ask the abbot about the broken bridge. Youbai demands an infallible original. The abbot unrolls a map patched upon patches.
S00-05.objective: Ask the abbot to check the old bridge and mountain-route records
S00-05.result: The abbot confirms the old bridge is gone and a new route exists. He permits corrections based on firsthand evidence.
lines: Bring out the original, Abbot. Copies may be wrong. Surely the original is sound.
The abbot unfolds a map. Beneath one layer is another. Old bridges, new bridges, and detours overlap like a patchwork robe.
That original gets a lot of mending.
Bridges fell, streams rose, paths changed. Whenever someone walked a route themselves, we added a note.
Then... which layer did the ancestors settle on?
The one they walked. The one you walked today may become a layer too.
Youbai moves aside, exposing the crooked note it guarded so fiercely. The abbot confirms the old bridge is gone; the pine-root steps are the current route.
I see. Respecting our predecessors doesn't stop us from getting this next line right.

S00-06.title: Complete the Tiantai Map
S00-06.summary: Youbai still wants a credit line. But as you carefully strike out the wrong route, the spirit quietly lights the empty corner for you.
S00-06.objective: Make the first correction to the Tiantai route
S00-06.result: The Tiantai map is complete. You receive a new lead about Huangshan's hidden stream.
lines: Old bridge crossed out. Stone steps added. Leave a corner for who saw it and when it changed.
Start that corner with: Under Youbai's excellent guidance.
Certainly. Then: Briefly recommended takeoff from a collapsed bridge.
Youbai falls silent, then moves its light to your brush. Beside the new route, the crooked old note seems less glaring.
Mark the wrong route too. The next traveler shouldn't have to repeat the mistake.
Now you sound like a guardian of maps.
With the Tiantai map complete, the abbot gives you a record of Huangshan's hidden stream. The same stretch of water appears in two different forms.
Elder, next time let's work out which drawing is wrong before we argue over the credits.

S00-07.title: The Inn
S00-07.summary: The innkeeper makes the bridge detour sound mysterious, then offers a guaranteed map for a fee. You look down: the evidence is supporting his backside.
S00-07.objective: Check mountain-route and lodging rumors with the innkeeper
S00-07.result: The innkeeper confirms the detour. You learn to record rumors separately from firsthand evidence.
lines: We offer tea and directions. Directions cost extra. Guaranteed directions cost extra again.
Then start by guaranteeing which of your two opposite routes is the real one.
Agreed. Prices may have tiers. Mountain paths should not have doubles.
The innkeeper shifts his stool, revealing part of an old bridge rail beneath a leg. You recognize the broken wooden joint.
So the bridge didn't retire. It took a desk job here.
Salvaged bridge timber! When the pilgrims switched to the steps, I moved my trade to meet them.
You have him point out the detour, matching the timber with what you saw along the road. The hand waiting for money turns to pouring tea.
This pot is on me. Hear plenty of rumors, but look twice before you write. Don't follow my example: more talk than directions.
